questions.stem: Why are departmental accounts important for a business?

options.text: To evaluate the performance of each department.
To reduce the overall tax liability.
To increase the sales of the business.
To eliminate the need for financial audits.

questions.explanation: Departmental accounts are crucial for evaluating the performance of each department, helping management make informed decisions.

distractorRationale.b: Reducing tax liability is not a primary function of departmental accounts.
distractorRationale.c: Increasing sales is a result of marketing strategies, not departmental accounts.
distractorRationale.d: Financial audits are still necessary regardless of departmental accounts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common basis for apportioning rent expense between departments?
questions.explanation: Rent is typically apportioned based on the floor space occupied by each department, as it directly relates to the cost incurred.

distractorRationale.a: Number of employees is more relevant for apportioning salaries.
distractorRationale.c: Sales volume is used for apportioning marketing expenses.
distractorRationale.d: Cost of goods sold is not related to rent expenses.

questions.stem: What is the first step in preparing a departmental trading and profit and loss account?
questions.explanation: The first step is to record sales and purchases for each department, as this forms the basis of the trading account.

distractorRationale.a: Apportioning indirect expenses is done after recording sales and purchases.
distractorRationale.c: Allocating direct expenses follows the recording of sales and purchases.
distractorRationale.d: Calculating net profit is the final step after all expenses have been accounted for.

questions.stem: Explain how a business can use departmental accounts to improve resource allocation.
markingGuide: Reallocate resources to more profitable departments (2 marks).
Use data to make informed decisions (1 mark).
questions.explanation: Departmental accounts provide detailed financial data that helps management identify which departments are underperforming and which are more profitable, enabling better resource allocation.
